chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, son of Yahya, from Ahmad, son of Muhammad, from Maruk, son of Ubayd, from Rifa'ah, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

He said: 'Do you know, O Rifa'ah, why the believer is called a believer?' I said, 'I do not know.' He said: 'Because he entrusts himself to Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, so Allah validates his safety/guarantee.'

key_terms.يُؤْمِنُ عَلَى اللَّهِ: He entrusts himself to Allah / He believes in Allah's guarantee

ai.seo_question: Why is a Muslim called a 'believer' (Mu'min) according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In this hadith from Al-Kafi, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) elucidates that the term 'mu'min' derives from the root 'amanah' (trust/security), signifying that the believer places trust in Allah, who in turn guarantees their safety. This concept highlights the reciprocal covenant between the Divine and the faithful, a key theme in Shia theology regarding divine assurance on the Day of Judgment. The narration underscores that true faith is not merely belief but a state of being secured by God's promise.

en.hubeali: H 14609 – Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Marouk Bin Ubeyd, from Rafa’at, who has narrated the following: Abu Abdullahasws

having said: ‘Do you know, O Rafa’at, why the ‘الْمُؤْمِنُ’ Believer is called ‘Momin’?’ I said, ‘I do not know’. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Because he entrusts himself to Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Mighty and Majestic, so Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Authorises safety for him’.
en.sarwar: 161. Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Marouk Bin Ubeyd, from Rafa’at, who has narrated the following: Abu Abdullah (a.s.) having said:

‘Do you know, O Rafa’at, why the ‘الْمُؤْمِنُ’ Believer is called ‘Momin’?’ I said, ‘I do not know’. He (a.s.) said: ‘Because he entrusts himself to Allah (azwj) Mighty and Majestic, so Allah (azwj) Authorises safety for him’.
